eligibility_reason: The paper reports self-reported prevalence of sharing/amplifying exaggerated or false news among UK social media users and political-news sharers. The estimates are survey recall measures rather than observed platform shares.

estimates.denominator: UK social media users who shared political news in the past month (n=589)
estimates.measure: share who self-reported amplifying exaggerated or false news
estimates.misinfo_definition: Exaggerated or false news shared without providing information to correct inaccuracies
estimates.source_quote: As Table 1 shows, a third (33.8%) of UK social media users who shared news in the past month amplified exaggerated or false news (RQ1).
estimates.notes: Self-reported survey measure; the paper calls this amplification.

estimates.measure: share who self-reported amplifying exaggerated or false news
estimates.misinfo_definition: Exaggerated or false news shared without providing information to correct inaccuracies
estimates.source_quote: This amounts to a tenth (9.9%) of all UK social media users—a substantial minority, especially if one considers social desirability bias in a survey and how strictly we defined amplification.
estimates.notes: Self-reported survey measure; the paper calls this amplification.

estimates.denominator: UK social media users who shared political news in the past month (n=589)
estimates.measure: share who reported sharing news that seemed accurate at the time but was later found to be made up
estimates.misinfo_definition: News that seemed accurate at the time but was later found to be made up; retained as amplification when not corrected
estimates.source_quote: Seemed accurate at the time, but you later found out was made-up 52 8.8

estimates.denominator: UK social media users who shared political news in the past month (n=589)
estimates.measure: share who reported sharing exaggerated news without being aware of the exaggeration
estimates.misinfo_definition: Exaggerated news shared without providing information to correct inaccuracies
estimates.source_quote: This was the case for 14.8% of all those who shared political news.
estimates.notes: Self-reported survey measure; the paper says respondents later found the content problematic.

estimates.denominator: UK social media users who shared political news in the past month (n=589)
estimates.measure: share who reported sharing exaggerated news while aware of the exaggeration
estimates.misinfo_definition: Exaggerated news shared without providing information to correct inaccuracies
estimates.source_quote: Was exaggerated, and you were aware of this 15 2.5

estimates.denominator: UK social media users who shared political news in the past month (n=589)
estimates.measure: share who reported sharing news they thought was made up when they shared it
estimates.misinfo_definition: Made-up news shared without providing information to correct inaccuracies
estimates.source_quote: 7.6% of sharers said they knowingly amplified made-up news.
estimates.notes: Self-reported survey measure; the paper calls this knowingly amplified made-up news.
